en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of 7,641 islands, of which only about 2,000 are permanently inhabited.
The Philippine Senate consists of exactly 24 senators who are elected nationally to serve a single six-year term.
The Philippines recognizes over 180 living languages, but Filipino and English serve as the two official national languages.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution contains 18 articles, with Article III specifically outlining the Bill of Rights for all citizens.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote exactly two major novels, Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo, before his execution at age 35.
The Lumad consist of about 18 distinct indigenous ethnolinguistic groups living across the southern island of Mindanao.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a traditional two-step forward and one-step backward dance.
National Scientist Dr. Angel Alcala discovered exactly 51 new species of reptiles and amphibians in the Philippines.
The Philippine national gem is the pearl, featuring the massive 34-kilogram Pearl of Puerto Princesa discovered in 1934.
The smallest local government unit in the Philippines is the barangay, and the country currently has over 42,000 barangays.
The Philippine flag features three yellow stars representing the three principal geographic island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Dr. Fe del Mundo became the first female student admitted to Harvard Medical School, graduating after a four-year program.
